text: dsh-coding-discipline 为 DSH 添加 Coding agent 预设和可供 profile 中 agent 加载的 coding-discipline skill。插件把 Markdown skill 注册到 skills 服务，bundle 同时插入 Coding persona 预设。该流程强调先读任务和相关代码、保持最小改动、依据项目自身标准验证，并在完成时报告证据。适合希望统一编码 agent 工作步骤的用户；不需要额外密钥或外部账号。

dsh-coding-discipline adds a Coding preset and a loadable coding skill to DSH. It registers the embedded skill and adds a persona preset that guides agents to read first, make minimal edits, verify with project checks, and report evidence. No extra key or account is needed.
想让编码 agent 修改前先读清任务和相关代码。
有没有办法要求 agent 只做最小必要改动并保留现有接口？
I want my coding agent to verify changes with the repository's actual checks and report what it observed.
dsh-coding-discipline 的功能「编码流程 skill」：通过 skills 服务提供可加载的编码指南，涵盖先读任务、最小改动、项目检查验证和证据报告。

dsh-coding-discipline README · dsh-coding-discipline：Coding-discipline enhancement for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`).

This plugin ships two pieces that work together:

dsh-coding-discipline README · dsh-coding-discipline：1. **A `Coding` agent preset** (`id: coding`) — the shipped `standard` preset's plugin list with the **same tools**
   and a strengthened persona: verify-first edits, minimal diffs, real test runs, no test gaming, spec-only
   verification, and evidence-based reports. No new tools, no permission changes, so it is comparable with the
   baseline and safe to switch back.
2. **An embedded `coding-discipline` skill** — the full procedure behind the preset contract, registered at host
   level so any agent in the profile can discover and load it on demand. Project/user skills with the same name
   still win by rank.

dsh-coding-discipline README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-coding-discipline
```

From GitHub instead of npm:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:JinBeiCN/dsh-coding-discipline
```

Install from the release tarball if neither route is available:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/JinBeiCN/dsh-coding-discipline/releases/download/v1.0.0/dsh-coding-discipline-1.0.0.tgz
```

Then use it:

dsh-coding-discipline README · Install：- **New sessions:** choose **Coding** in the agent-preset selector. To make it the default for new sessions,
  set it in Settings → General (Agent preset).
- **Any session:** the `coding-discipline` skill is listed in the skill catalog; load it before coding work.
  Existing sessions are not changed by installing the bundle.

dsh-coding-discipline README · Measured behaviour (plain statement)：The preset was evaluated against an uninjected baseline on a self-built 16-task coding benchmark with
`deepseek-flash` (`reasoningEffort=max`), 18 isolated agent runs per arm:

dsh-coding-discipline README · Measured behaviour (plain statement)：So this plugin is a **guardrail**, not a capability booster: it changes how work is done and reported, and it
matters most for weaker models, lower reasoning effort, long specs, or review-heavy delivery. It does not make an
already-saturated model produce more correct code in our benchmark.

dsh-coding-discipline README · Compatibility：- `dsh` `>=0.2.1-rc.2`, Node.js `>=18`.
- Web and Desktop profiles with the agent-preset registry (the shipped `standard` preset must be present, which
  it is in the default `web` profile). Headless/ACP profiles have no preset registry and do not load the preset
  part; the embedded skill part is registered wherever the bundle's host row is mounted.

dsh-coding-discipline README · Size and token cost：- Persona: 325 words, charged per request only in sessions that select the `Coding` preset.
- Embedded skill: 7,600 characters of body (7,923 including frontmatter), below the standard preset's
  8,000-character skill budget; it is only charged when a session loads the skill.
- No tools are added or removed.

dsh-coding-discipline README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-coding-discipline
```

Disabling the bundle (or removing it) leaves existing sessions untouched until they are re-created.

dsh-coding-discipline README · Development：```sh
node --input-type=module -e "import('./index.js').then(m => console.log(m.name, m.inject))"
```

`index.js` exports a plain Cordis plugin (`name`, `inject`, `apply`) that registers the skill from
`skills/coding-discipline/SKILL.md`; `cordis.patch.yml` inserts that host row plus the `Coding` preset.
No build step and no runtime dependencies.
